quiet_o_x_centre_gate: A ReLU gate that switches on when o has few open singles and open twos while x holds the centre column, and when on raises x's predicted chance of winning. It is on for {{q:q_bb538a9e33.subgroup.n|d}} of the {{q:q_bb538a9e33.n_total|d}} training positions (a share of {{q:q_bb538a9e33.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}); on those positions x wins with perfect play at a rate of {{q:q_bb538a9e33.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} and the model's mean predicted chance is {{q:q_bb538a9e33.subgroup.mean_predicted_risk|pct}}, against an outcome rate of {{q:q_bb538a9e33.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest. Its largest terms are negative weights on o's open singles and open twos and a positive weight on x's centre pieces (closed form in the analytical_formula record, rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[0].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}} on the training rows). Reading: the concept 'x's centre pieces minus o's open singles minus o's open twos' predicts the gate being on with AUC {{q:q_20245a91cd.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_20245a91cd.score|.2f}}, meaningful). Self-probe: with x holding two centre pieces at the typical case, the gate's value falls as o's open singles rise from a count of 0 to 8, from {{q:q_c777136f83.rows[0].nodes.1.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_c777136f83.rows[8].nodes.1.value|.2f}}, and the whole-model predicted chance falls from {{q:q_c777136f83.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_c777136f83.rows[8].risk|pct}}; at the typical case itself (x without a centre piece) the gate is off from o's open singles at a count of 7 upward (value {{q:q_389925b6ef.rows[7].nodes.1.value|.2f}}). Switching the part off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_03ce07aec2.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_03ce07aec2.data.auc_without|.4f}} and the part raises the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_03ce07aec2.data.mean_risk_change|.3f}} (whole model, mean over the training rows). The threat features enter with small weights and are not read here.
o_lines_ramp: A ReLU unit that is on for most positions ({{q:q_f919394d1a.units[4].active_fraction|.1%}} of the training rows) and acts as a ramp: its value falls as o's open singles, o's open twos and x's open twos grow, and rises with o's centre pieces and the number of odd-row playable columns; it feeds the output positively, so through this part o's line presence lowers x's predicted chance. o's threats act as a switch: a single o threat turns it off at the typical case (value {{q:q_daf2178e5e.rows[1].nodes.2.value|.2f}} with one o threat against {{q:q_daf2178e5e.rows[0].nodes.2.value|.2f}} with o's threat count at 0), and on the training rows {{q:q_af74cf9c6e.subgroup.n|d}} of the {{q:q_10b17cb77a.subgroup.n|d}} positions with an o threat have the unit on. Self-probe: at the typical case the unit falls from {{q:q_389925b6ef.rows[0].nodes.2.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_389925b6ef.rows[8].nodes.2.value|.2f}} as o's open singles rise from 0 to 8, and from {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[0].nodes.2.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[6].nodes.2.value|.2f}} as o's open twos rise from 0 to 6, while the whole-model predicted chance falls from {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[6].risk|pct}} over that sweep. Reading: the composite 'o's open singles + o's open twos + x's open twos + o's threats - o's centre pieces' predicts the unit being on with AUC {{q:q_f1fc518ba9.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_f1fc518ba9.score|.2f}}); a reading in terms of o's open lines alone ('o's open singles + o's open twos') scores {{q:q_5f39cd838c.score|.2f}}, so the game reading is partial and the composite is close to the formula in words. This is the largest part: switching it off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_0546f55175.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_0546f55175.data.auc_without|.4f}}, and the part raises the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_0546f55175.data.mean_risk_change|.3f}} (whole model). Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[1].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
x_open_twos_cap: A ReLU unit that falls as x's open twos grow and is cut off at its floor; because it feeds the output with a negative weight, x's open twos raise x's predicted chance through this part until the unit reaches the floor, after which further open twos add nothing through this part. The unit is at its floor on {{q:q_153f133c71.subgroup.n|d}} of the {{q:q_153f133c71.n_total|d}} training positions ({{q:q_153f133c71.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), where x wins at a rate of {{q:q_153f133c71.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} against {{q:q_153f133c71.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest. The cap is near two open twos: of the {{q:q_7260771b28.subgroup.n|d}} positions with at least two x open twos, {{q:q_f31d9a99f1.subgroup.n|d}} still have the unit on, and {{q:q_759ff5b160.subgroup.n|d}} positions with fewer than two have it already at the floor (the other inputs, mainly o's centre pieces, odd-row playable columns and the threat counts, move the cut-off). Self-probe at the typical case: as x's open twos rise from 0 to 6 the unit goes {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[0].nodes.3.value|.2f}}, {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[1].nodes.3.value|.2f}}, {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[2].nodes.3.value|.2f}} and stays at the floor; the whole-model predicted chance rises from {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[2].risk|pct}} over the first two open twos and then more slowly, to {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[6].risk|pct}} at six, because the direct term keeps rising while the other units reading x's open twos reach their own floors. A single o threat also turns this unit off at the typical case (value {{q:q_daf2178e5e.rows[1].nodes.3.value|.2f}}). Reading: x's open twos predict the unit being on with AUC {{q:q_9d23235624.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_9d23235624.score|.2f}}, meaningful). Switching the part off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_6d52a0a56f.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_6d52a0a56f.data.auc_without|.4f}}; the part lowers the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_6d52a0a56f.data.mean_abs_risk_change|.3f}} on average (whole model). Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[2].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
o_centre_x_singles_gate: A ReLU gate that switches on when o holds the centre column while x has many open singles and few centre pieces, and when on raises x's predicted chance. It is on for {{q:q_94ce0c01d7.subgroup.n|d}} of the {{q:q_94ce0c01d7.n_total|d}} training positions ({{q:q_94ce0c01d7.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), where x wins at a rate of {{q:q_94ce0c01d7.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} against {{q:q_94ce0c01d7.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest; its value when on is small, so its whole-model effect is small: switching it off changes the training AUC from {{q:q_563c5c19ab.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_563c5c19ab.data.auc_without|.4f}}, and the part raises the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_563c5c19ab.data.mean_risk_change|.3f}}. Self-probe: with o holding two centre pieces and x's centre count at 0 at the typical case, the gate turns on as x's open singles rise (off at three singles, value {{q:q_9ed7bf4983.rows[4].nodes.7.value|.2f}} at four and {{q:q_9ed7bf4983.rows[10].nodes.7.value|.2f}} at ten) while the whole-model chance rises from {{q:q_9ed7bf4983.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_9ed7bf4983.rows[10].risk|pct}}; sweeping o's centre pieces at the typical case the gate is off at 0 and 1 centre piece and on from 2 (value {{q:q_4a8088b017.rows[2].nodes.7.value|.2f}}, rising to {{q:q_4a8088b017.rows[4].nodes.7.value|.2f}} at 4). The gate is also on for {{q:q_47a411b467.subgroup.n|d}} positions in which o's centre count is 0 (x's open singles alone can switch it). Reading: 'o's centre pieces + x's open singles - x's centre pieces' predicts the gate being on with AUC {{q:q_1d9d355bc3.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_1d9d355bc3.score|.2f}}, partial); the reading holds for part of its behaviour. Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[3].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
centre_column_block: Three coupled ReLU units reading the centre column, plus a copy of the x-singles-vs-twos gate (10_b) that feeds the heavy-centre gate with a small weight. Unit 6 rises with the pieces of either side in the centre column (o's and x's centre pieces have the two largest weights) and feeds the output weakly; it is on for {{q:q_f919394d1a.units[7].active_fraction|.1%}} of the training rows. Unit 76 (the heavy-centre gate) is driven by unit 6; it switches on when the centre column is heavily occupied and lowers x's predicted chance strongly. It is on for {{q:q_84309de234.subgroup.n|d}} positions ({{q:q_84309de234.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), where x wins at {{q:q_84309de234.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} against {{q:q_84309de234.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest; the rule 'at least three centre pieces in total' matches it except for {{q:q_d57625fccd.subgroup.n|d}} positions on which it is on with fewer and {{q:q_05df13e859.subgroup.n|d}} on which it is off with three or more (of {{q:q_7a42576b21.subgroup.n|d}} such positions). Unit 4 switches on when x holds the centre (x's centre pieces and unit 6 are its largest positive terms, with o's open singles and twos) and raises x's predicted chance; it is on for {{q:q_74fd50a969.subgroup.n|d}} positions ({{q:q_74fd50a969.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), of which {{q:q_6052d55945.subgroup.n|d}} have fewer than two x centre pieces. Self-probe (grid of centre pieces at the typical case): with x holding three centre pieces and o holding 0, unit 4 is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[3].nodes.4.value|.2f}}, unit 76 is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[3].nodes.76.value|.2f}} and the whole-model chance is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[3].risk|pct}}; with two pieces each, unit 76 is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[10].nodes.76.value|.2f}} and the chance is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[10].risk|pct}}; with o holding three and x one the chance is {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[13].risk|pct}}, against {{q:q_f6f612d381.rows[0].risk|pct}} with an empty centre column. So the block reads: x in the centre is good for x, but a crowded centre column (whichever side crowds it) lowers x's predicted chance. Reading: the total of centre pieces predicts the three exits being on with mean AUC {{q:q_f5ab374baa.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_f5ab374baa.score|.2f}}, meaningful). Switching the block off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_acc8e477c6.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_acc8e477c6.data.auc_without|.4f}}; the block changes the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_acc8e477c6.data.mean_risk_change|.3f}} with a mean absolute change of {{q:q_acc8e477c6.data.mean_abs_risk_change|.3f}} (whole model). Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[5].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
x_lines_vs_o_centre_pair: Two ReLU units reading x's open lines against o's centre pieces and open lines, sharing a copy of o's open threes through unit 2510, which is positive on {{q:q_09a02b83d8.subgroup.share_of_rows|.0%}} of the training rows ({{q:q_09a02b83d8.subgroup.n|d}} of {{q:q_09a02b83d8.n_total|d}}) and so acts as an affine pass-through of o's open threes into both units. Unit 8 rises with x's open singles and falls with o's centre pieces and o's open singles and twos; it is on for {{q:q_f919394d1a.units[10].active_fraction|.1%}} of the rows and feeds the output positively. Unit 9 rises when x has few open singles and open twos and o is out of the centre; it is on for {{q:q_816b7ed147.subgroup.n|d}} positions ({{q:q_816b7ed147.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), where x wins at {{q:q_816b7ed147.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} against {{q:q_816b7ed147.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest, and feeds the output negatively. Both therefore raise x's predicted chance when x has more open lines; on the {{q:q_12e16bf579.subgroup.n|d}} positions where unit 8 is off and unit 9 is on, x wins at {{q:q_12e16bf579.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}}. Self-probe at the typical case: as x's open singles rise from 0 to 10, unit 8 rises from {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[0].nodes.8.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[10].nodes.8.value|.2f}}, unit 9 falls from {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[0].nodes.9.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[10].nodes.9.value|.2f}}, and the whole-model chance rises from {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[10].risk|pct}}; as o's centre pieces rise from 0 to 3, unit 8 falls from {{q:q_4a8088b017.rows[0].nodes.8.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_4a8088b017.rows[3].nodes.8.value|.2f}}. Reading: 'x's open singles + x's open twos - o's open singles - o's centre pieces' predicts the two exits with mean AUC {{q:q_4dc72ff87e.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_4dc72ff87e.score|.2f}}, partial): the reading holds for part of the pair's behaviour; unit 9 in particular mixes x's line counts with o's centre pieces and parity terms and is described by its closed form rather than explained. Switching the pair off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_596e1748b2.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_596e1748b2.data.auc_without|.4f}} with a mean absolute change in predicted chance of {{q:q_596e1748b2.data.mean_abs_risk_change|.3f}} (whole model). Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[6].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
direct_terms: The direct linear terms, collected at an identity node: a weighted sum of seven inputs passed straight to the output's logit. Per standard deviation of the input, x's open twos add {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[0].weight|.2f}} to the logit directly, o's open singles add {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[1].weight|.2f}}, o's open twos {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[2].weight|.2f}}, o's centre pieces {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[3].weight|.2f}}, x's open singles {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[4].weight|.2f}}, even-row playable columns {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[5].weight|.2f}} and x's open threes {{q:q_3b1023aa31.switched_off[6].weight|.2f}} (these are the edge weights, the direct effects; the whole-model effect of each input also runs through the ReLU parts, for instance x's open twos through the x-open-twos cap). The exit is dominated by x's open twos: that input alone explains an R-squared of {{q:q_b7ef1b91f6.r2|.2f}} of the exit (score {{q:q_b7ef1b91f6.score|.2f}}, meaningful). Self-probe at the typical case: as x's open twos rise from 0 to 6 the exit rises from {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[0].nodes.identity_0.value|.2f}} to {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[6].nodes.identity_0.value|.2f}}. Switching the direct terms off together (exit fixed at its mean) lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_774244c73d.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_774244c73d.data.auc_without|.4f}} with a mean absolute change in predicted chance of {{q:q_774244c73d.data.mean_abs_risk_change|.3f}}. The closed form is in the analytical_formula record (a linear sum; its rounded coefficients are off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[7].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
win_probability_root: The output is the sigmoid of an additive logit: the eight parts (seven ReLU parts and the direct linear terms) each add a weighted exit value, and the parts combine by addition at the output (function preservation of the refactored model: max error {{q:q_fdd92cec67.function_preservation_max_abs_err|.1e}}). On the training split the model has AUC {{q:q_9a1dea33fd.auc_roc|.3f}} and accuracy {{q:q_9a1dea33fd.accuracy|.3f}}; replacing each nonlinear unit by its affine fit leaves AUC {{q:q_ce159c271d.auc_all_affine|.3f}} (a nonlinear gain of {{q:q_ce159c271d.nonlinear_gain|.3f}}), so the model is largely a weighted sum of line features with a few gates and caps. Main effects: x's open twos raise x's predicted chance (directly and through the x-open-twos cap, which saturates near two open twos: whole-model chance {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[0].risk|pct}}, {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[2].risk|pct}} and {{q:q_652fe92047.rows[6].risk|pct}} at 0, 2 and 6 open twos at the typical case); x's open singles raise it (chance {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[0].risk|pct}} at 0 to {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[10].risk|pct}} at 10, through the x-lines-vs-o-centre pair, the x-singles-vs-twos gate and the o-centre-x-singles gate); o's open singles and open twos lower it (chance {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_3e23718b44.rows[6].risk|pct}} as o's open twos go from 0 to 6, through the o-lines ramp, the quiet-o gate and the pair). Gates: a single o threat switches the o-lines ramp and the x-open-twos cap off and drops the chance to {{q:q_daf2178e5e.rows[1].risk|pct}} from {{q:q_daf2178e5e.rows[0].risk|pct}} at the typical case; the centre column block raises the chance when x holds the centre and lowers it when the centre column is crowded by either side (heavy-centre gate). The largest parts by AUC loss when switched off are the o-lines ramp ({{q:q_0546f55175.data.auc_without|.4f}}), the x-open-twos cap ({{q:q_6d52a0a56f.data.auc_without|.4f}}) and the direct terms ({{q:q_774244c73d.data.auc_without|.4f}}), against {{q:q_9a1dea33fd.auc_roc|.4f}} with everything on. x's threats coincide with x's open threes on the training rows ({{q:q_8aff1dd0f2.subgroup.n|d}} rows differ) and o's threats with o's open threes ({{q:q_52825987c4.subgroup.n|d}} rows differ); both are rare ({{q:q_efdd0b4e0e.subgroup.n|d}} and {{q:q_10b17cb77a.subgroup.n|d}} positions), and the parity splits of threats are rarer still ({{q:q_4cb3bce25e.subgroup.n|d}} positions with an x odd-row threat, {{q:q_9a8a256c0c.subgroup.n|d}} with an o odd-row threat), so their weights are fitted to few rows and are described, not explained. The sixteen inputs are each connected and enter through split copies, one per part.
x_singles_vs_twos_gate: A ReLU gate that rises with x's open singles and falls with x's open twos, the number of even-row playable columns and x's odd-row threats; when on it raises x's predicted chance. It is on for {{q:q_8d908f25d4.subgroup.n|d}} of the {{q:q_8d908f25d4.n_total|d}} training positions ({{q:q_8d908f25d4.subgroup.share_of_rows|.1%}}), where x wins at {{q:q_8d908f25d4.subgroup.outcome_rate|.1%}} against {{q:q_8d908f25d4.rest.outcome_rate|.1%}} on the rest. The gate is rarely on when x's open singles are fewer than x's open twos plus the even-row playable columns ({{q:q_0a0e613a5b.subgroup.n|d}} such positions on the training rows), but that condition is far from sufficient: the gate is off on {{q:q_b48c668606.subgroup.n|d}} positions that satisfy it, because the threshold in counts is much higher than the sum (the weights are per standard deviation and the inputs have different spreads). Self-probe at the typical case: the gate is off up to seven x open singles and on from eight (value {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[8].nodes.10_a.value|.2f}} at eight, {{q:q_3ec085ab1a.rows[10].nodes.10_a.value|.2f}} at ten); sweeping even-row playable columns it falls from {{q:q_d3357436c8.rows[0].nodes.10_a.value|.2f}} at 0 to off from 3 upward, and the whole-model chance falls from {{q:q_d3357436c8.rows[0].risk|pct}} to {{q:q_d3357436c8.rows[7].risk|pct}} at 7 (the other units reading parity contribute too). Reading: 'x's open singles - x's open twos - even-row playable columns' predicts the gate being on with AUC {{q:q_52402e1ec7.auc|.2f}} (score {{q:q_52402e1ec7.score|.2f}}, meaningful). Switching the part off lowers the training AUC from {{q:q_6a40b83630.data.auc_with|.4f}} to {{q:q_6a40b83630.data.auc_without|.4f}}, and the part raises the mean predicted chance by {{q:q_6a40b83630.data.mean_risk_change|.3f}} (whole model). A copy of this unit (10_b) also feeds the heavy-centre gate inside the centre column block with a small weight. Closed form in the analytical_formula record (rounded; off by at most {{q:q_fdd92cec67.leaves[4].closed_form_max_abs_err|.2g}}).
